```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "C.UTF-8"))
library(data.table)
library(DT)
A <- "docs/assets/isolaser_gtex"
st <- fread(file.path(A, "fig3e_style_stats.tsv"))
pts <- fread(file.path(A, "fig3e_style_points.tsv"))
fun <- fread(file.path(A, "fig3e_style_funnel.tsv"))
cascade <- fread(file.path(A, "filter_cascade.tsv"))
PAPER <- "Paper's cutoff"; BEFORE <- "Before FDR"; AFTER <- "After FDR"
SET_ORDER <- c(PAPER, BEFORE, AFTER)
tpl <- function(x) sub("hr", " hr", x)
strong <- pts[set == BEFORE & pval_nominal < 1e-5]
sigpairs <- pts[gtex_significant_pair == TRUE]
```

We compare our allelic splicing effects (isoLASER ΔPSI) with GTEx v8
Cerebellum sQTL effects (beta), as in the right panel of
[Fig. 3e of the isoLASER paper](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-64605-6).
As in the paper, we use the **skipping junction** of each event, whose usage
falls when the exonic part is included, so a **negative correlation** is
expected.

# How pairs were matched

- **Variant and gene:** the same SNV (position, REF and ALT; isoLASER's
  0-based position + 1 = GTEx's) tested for the same Ensembl gene in GTEx.
- **GTEx data:** full Cerebellum summary statistics, every tested association
  at any p-value. 
- **Event:** the exonic part must form an annotated exon-skipping or
  alternative-splice-site event (the cluster types the paper used), and the
  GTEx junction must be exactly that event's skipping junction.
- **Points:** each point is one **pair**: an isoLASER association (variant ×
  exonic part) and its matched GTEx skipping junction, at one timepoint.
  Timepoints are plotted separately.
- **Our associations**, three sets (see the next section):
  - **Paper's cutoff:** isoLASER's own `cis` label and pooled ΔPSI, as in the
    paper;
  - **Before FDR:** our screen (heterozygous donors only, ≥ 30 reads, `cis`,
    |ΔPSI| ≥ 0.10, part ≥ 10 bp, no other variant within 30 bp);
  - **After FDR:** our screen plus permutation BH q < 0.05 within each
    timepoint, as on the [FDR page](isolaser_fdr.html).

**Example, HNRNPK.** The C>T variant (chr9:83980154, 0-based) and the 34-base
exonic part (gold) form an alternative splice site. GTEx measures the
skipping junction (blue), which jumps over the part; the grey junction
includes it. At 6 hours, ALT changes part inclusion by
`r sprintf("%+.1f", 100*pts[set == BEFORE & tp == "6hr" & gene == "HNRNPK" & variant_qual == "chr9:83980154:C>T", dpsi])`
percentage points, and GTEx's beta for the skipping junction is
`r sprintf("%+.2f", pts[set == BEFORE & tp == "6hr" & gene == "HNRNPK" & variant_qual == "chr9:83980154:C>T", slope])`:
opposite signs, as expected.

![](assets/isolaser_gtex/comparable_event_example_skipping.png)

```{r funnel}
f <- fun[order(match(set, SET_ORDER), tp), .(Set=set, Timepoint=tpl(tp),
             `Our associations (SNVs)`=reported_snv_associations, `Same variant and gene tested in GTEx`=tested_in_gtex,
             `Plotted pairs`=plotted, Genes=genes)]
knitr::kable(f, align="llrrrr")
```

**Our associations (SNVs)**: variant × exonic part associations with a
single-base variant at that timepoint. **Same variant and gene tested in
GTEx**: of those, the ones whose variant is tested for the same gene in GTEx
Cerebellum. **Plotted pairs**: association × matched GTEx skipping junction.

# Our cutoffs versus the paper's

The paper used isoLASER's own `cis` calls. Our screen adds five filters, so it
starts from far fewer associations (all three timepoints together):

```{r cascade}
knitr::kable(cascade[, .(Step=step, Associations=format(associations, big.mark=","), Genes=format(genes, big.mark=","),
                         `Used in the paper`=paper)], align="lrrl")
```

**Associations**: distinct variant × exonic part pairs at any timepoint. The
heterozygous-only rows come from the original isoLASER run's depth comparison;
the others from the rerun used for the permutation test (the two runs agree
closely). Each filter has a reason: below 30 reads, variant calls disagree
more often with the genotype panel; heterozygous donors keep the comparison
within each person, whereas pooling homozygous donors compares people; and
clustered variant calls are excluded as a conservative precaution, which can
also remove real variants.

```{r stats}
s <- dcast(st[subset %in% c("all", "GTEx p < 1e-5")], set + tp ~ subset, value.var=c("n", "expected_sign", "pearson_r", "pearson_p"))
s <- s[order(match(set, SET_ORDER), tp), .(Set=set, Timepoint=tpl(tp),
           `Pairs`=n_all, `All: R (p)`=sprintf("%.2f (%s)", pearson_r_all, vapply(pearson_p_all, function(x) format(signif(x, 2)), "")),
           `All: expected sign`=sprintf("%d/%d", expected_sign_all, n_all),
           `GTEx p < 1e-5: expected sign`=fifelse(is.na(`n_GTEx p < 1e-5`), "none", sprintf("%d/%d", `expected_sign_GTEx p < 1e-5`, `n_GTEx p < 1e-5`)))]
knitr::kable(s, align="llrrrr")
```

## Direction where GTEx is significant (paper's cutoff)

We take the paper's-cutoff pairs where GTEx is significant (nominal
p < 0.05, the blue points in the top row). A pair is **consistent** when our
ΔPSI and GTEx's beta have opposite signs, the expected negative relation for a
skipping junction. A binomial test asks whether the share of consistent pairs
differs from 50%, the share expected if directions were unrelated. These
definitions are our own; the paper reports only the correlation.

```{r consistency}
blue <- pts[set == PAPER & pval_nominal < 0.05 & dpsi != 0]
once <- blue[, .(dpsi=mean(dpsi), slope=slope[1]), by=.(Gene_name, variant_qual, exonic_part, phenotype_id)]
bt <- function(d) {
  k <- sum(d$dpsi * d$slope < 0); n <- nrow(d)
  data.table(Pairs=n, Consistent=k, `Consistent (%)`=round(100 * k / n),
             `Binomial p, two-sided`=signif(binom.test(k, n)$p.value, 2),
             `Binomial p, one-sided`=signif(binom.test(k, n, alternative="greater")$p.value, 2))
}
cons <- rbind(blue[order(tp), bt(.SD), by=.(Timepoint=tpl(tp))],
              data.table(Timepoint="All timepoints, every point", bt(blue)),
              data.table(Timepoint="All timepoints, each pair once", bt(once)))
knitr::kable(cons, align="lrrrrr")
```

At every timepoint slightly more than half of the pairs are consistent
(`r paste0(range(cons[1:3, "Consistent (%)"]), collapse="–")`%), and no
test reaches p < 0.05, whether the timepoints are tested separately or together.

**Pairs**: association × GTEx skipping junction with GTEx p < 0.05.
**Consistent**: pairs with opposite signs. **Two-sided p**: is the share
different from 50%. **One-sided p**: is it above 50%, the direction expected.
**Every point** counts each timepoint's points, so a pair called at two or
three timepoints counts two or three times and the points are not
independent. **Each pair once** counts every association × junction pair
once, using its mean ΔPSI over the timepoints where it is called. One point
with ΔPSI exactly 0 (CHGB, 6 hr) has no direction and is left out.

# Data

```{r points}
d <- pts[order(match(set, SET_ORDER), tp, gene), .(Set=set, Timepoint=tpl(tp), Gene=gene,
  Variant=variant_qual, `Exonic part`=exonic_part, `GTEx junction`=paste0(intron_start_0, "-", intron_end_0),
  `Our dPSI`=round(dpsi, 3), `Our BH q`=signif(q_bh, 2), `GTEx beta`=signif(slope, 3), `GTEx p`=signif(pval_nominal, 2))]
DT::datatable(as.data.frame(d), rownames=FALSE, filter="top", options=list(pageLength=10, scrollX=TRUE))
```

**Variant**: isoLASER's 0-based position. **GTEx junction**: 0-based,
half-open intron coordinates. Download the
[points](assets/isolaser_gtex/fig3e_style_points.tsv) and
[statistics](assets/isolaser_gtex/fig3e_style_stats.tsv).

Reproduce from `long_read_RNA/10.isolaser_permutation/`: for each set, run
`python 27.gtex_fdr_comparison.py --prepare-full-cerebellum` and then
`Rscript 34.extract_full_cerebellum.R`, adding `--before-fdr` or
`--paper-cutoff` to both for those sets; then `Rscript 36.plot_fig3e_style.R`
(figure and tables) and `Rscript 37.filter_cascade.R` (the cutoff table).
**Our BH q** is blank for the paper's-cutoff set, which has no permutation
test.
